high.title: Bank of Korea May Rate Decision This Week - Monetary Policy Committee Meeting and Press Conference Scheduled
high.summary: The Bank of Korea's critical May Monetary Policy Committee meeting is scheduled for Thursday, May 28th at 09:00, followed by Governor's press conference at 11:10. The central bank will release its monetary policy direction immediately after the meeting, along with the May 2026 Economic Outlook at 13:30. This timing is crucial as markets are pricing in potential rate hikes amid rising inflation pressures. The meeting comes as Q1 2026 International Investment Position data will also be released on Wednesday, providing additional context for external balance considerations. June 2026 Monetary Stabilization Bond issuance plans will be announced at 17:00, offering insights into the BOK's liquidity management strategy. FX and bond traders should prepare for significant volatility around these releases, particularly given current market expectations for policy tightening.

high.title: ANZ Forecasts 25bp BOK Rate Hike in May Citing Import Price Risks and Economic Strength
high.summary: ANZ economist Crystal Tan predicts the Bank of Korea will implement a 25bp rate hike at the May 28th meeting, driven by escalating import price pressures from persistent energy costs and won weakness. The bank cites inflation exceeding target with high probability of further increases, while solid economic growth from strong semiconductor exports provides policy space for tightening. Growing financial market stability concerns add urgency to preemptive action. This hawkish call from a major international bank reinforces market expectations for the start of a tightening cycle. KRW traders should note the emphasis on currency weakness as an inflation driver, suggesting rate hikes could provide won support. Bond investors face potential yield curve steepening if the central bank begins normalizing policy from current accommodative levels.

high.title: Barclays Expects BOK Rate Freeze with Hawkish Message, Predicts Split Vote
high.summary: Barclays economist Son Beom-ki forecasts the Bank of Korea will maintain the base rate at 2.50% while delivering hawkish forward guidance signaling preemptive tightening ahead. The bank projects 1-2 dissenting votes favoring hikes, with potential for a 3-3 split requiring the governor's casting vote in extreme scenarios. The six-month dot plot is expected to show strong bias toward 3.00% terminal rate despite initial freeze. This creates a complex scenario for markets - immediate dovish relief from no hike but hawkish repricing of the forward curve. KRW could face two-way volatility depending on whether markets focus on the near-term pause or medium-term tightening signals. Bond yields may rise on hawkish guidance even without immediate rate action, particularly in the front end of the curve.

high.title: Dollar-Won Pares Losses to 1,507.20 as US-Iran Ceasefire Talks Spark Military Tensions
high.summary: USD/KRW closed overnight trading at 1,507.20, down 10.00 won from Seoul market close but recovering 2.90 won from intraday lows. Despite growing expectations for US-Iran ceasefire MOU, continued military brinkmanship triggered market caution and safe-haven demand. The pair had fallen to 1,504.30 during regular trading on peace optimism but found support as negotiations remained incomplete. Weekend talks showed progress but differences persist on Iranian asset unfreezing and other details. This geopolitical volatility creates challenging conditions for KRW positioning, with risk-on moves from peace progress offset by uncertainty over implementation. The 1,505-1,510 range appears to be key technical support/resistance. Bond markets also face conflicting signals from geopolitical resolution versus domestic inflation pressures ahead of Thursday's BOK meeting.

medium.title: BOK Expected to Hike Rates Twice to 3.0% by Year-End, KED Survey Shows
medium.summary: Survey results indicate market expectations for two BOK rate hikes bringing the policy rate to 3.0% by year-end, reflecting consensus that the central bank will begin tightening cycle soon. This aligns with inflation pressures from US-Iran conflict driving energy costs and semiconductor export strength supporting growth. The survey reinforces bond market pricing for higher yields and potential KRW support from policy normalization.

medium.title: South Korean Banks' Won-Denominated Loan Delinquency Rate Falls to 0.56% in March
medium.summary: Banking sector loan quality improved with delinquency rates declining to 0.56% from 0.62% in February, ending three months of deterioration. The improvement was attributed to quarter-end effects as banks expanded disposal of non-performing loans. This strengthening of financial sector fundamentals supports the case for BOK monetary policy normalization.

medium.title: Manufacturing Sentiment Turns 'Optimistic' for First Time in 3 Years, 9 Months
medium.summary: The all-industry Composite Business Survey Index rose to 98.9 with next month outlook at 97.6, indicating strengthening business confidence. This marks the first optimistic reading in nearly four years, supporting the economic backdrop for potential BOK policy tightening and positive sentiment for Korean assets.

medium.title: US 2-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand, Yield at 4.071%
medium.summary: US 2-year Treasury auction settled at 4.071%, up 25.9bp from previous month and highest since February 2025, with solid bid-to-cover ratio of 2.64. Rising US yields create headwinds for Korean bonds and support USD strength against KRW, though solid auction demand suggests market appetite for higher yielding paper.

medium.title: Insurers' Loans Shrink While Bad Debts Rise - Soundness Warning
medium.summary: Insurance companies' loan balances fell 1.1 trillion won to 264.1 trillion won in Q1, with corporate lending declining while household loans increased. Non-performing loan ratios rose slightly, indicating some stress in the financial system that could influence BOK policy considerations around financial stability versus inflation control.
